article_title: Dissection in the 21(st) century: virtual tables versus traditional methods and their influence on medical students' perception - a systematic review.
citation: Telecan Teodora, Capraș Roxana-Denisa, Filip Gabriela Adriana, Bonea Maria, Crivii Carmen-Bianca. (2025). Dissection in the 21st century: virtual tables versus traditional methods and their influence on medical students' perception – a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07946-6
title: Use virtual dissection tables as a complement to, not a substitute for, cadaveric dissection within a multimodal curriculum
description: The review concludes that virtual dissection tables (VDTs) are best implemented as complementary components of anatomy education rather than replacements for cadaveric dissection. Students across studies did not support eliminating cadaver-based instruction, with "preference for VDT-exclusive learning remained low, reported by only 2.4–30.2% of students". The review recommends a "hybrid instructional model, combining the visual and interactive advantages of VDTs with realism and tactile experience of cadaveric dissection".
requirements: Access to both VDT technology and cadaveric dissection resources to support the hybrid model
constraints: VDTs lack tactile feedback; high implementation costs (up to $200,000 USD) and limited device availability restrict large-scale deployment
target_learners: Undergraduate medical, nursing, physiotherapy, and dental technology students
target_learning_goals: Human anatomy knowledge, including musculoskeletal and neuroanatomy
examples: Studies in the review report 87.9% of students opposing complete replacement of cadaveric dissection and 85.6% preferring a hybrid approach
